# Owned parent connection: host source results

The owned reader now supplies the nested parent evidence retained by forced
samples. This is diagnostic-only preparation for the actual admitted-range
max6325 resource failure. No SDK, VM, epoch reset, live observer or native
acceptance occurred. Object remains331/403; Read33 and Construction39 remain open.

The author and each independent CODE, Python and security reviewer ran **116
passing host tests** on Python3.15. Reviewer probes additionally covered partial
parent evidence, membership drift, unknown/stale parents, interruption/cleanup,
path-like census values, symlinks/FIFOs, hostile exception getters and avoiding
extra memory rows. The reviews report no findings. All five Python sources/tests
compile in memory; files stay below800 lines and functions at most50 lines.
No packages or optional linters were installed; guest execution remains NOT_RUN.

The [lossless inert history](family-history.jsonl.gz) preserves the architecture,
baseline, actual failure outputs, Phase1 investigations, final verification,
coverage, pipeline and three independent source reviews. Each UTF-8 record has
its exact byte length and SHA-256. Intermediate hashes do not supply every
intermediate source revision; archived snippets are historical data, not an SDK.

The predecessor compatibility test produced one parent-start assertion failure
and one deliberate file-read error. Independent tracing confirmed census order
was preserved: the old reader reached PID7 separately after child41, so it could
not recover the injected error as a nested parent observation. This was not a
fixture setup failure or LexLean semantic negative. Both cases pass with the
owned connection. A separate actual close-only counterexample failed before
repair: one parent-file cleanup OSError was misclassified as ordinary parent
loss. Opt-in cleanup grouping now makes it fatal without changing default reader
behavior or hiding the original exception.

Four separately planted defects all failed targeted assertions: disabling fatal
parent cleanup, dropping parent start, omitting the outer proc-root guard, and
excluding parent evidence from the identity fingerprint. One bounded reusable
source copy was removed afterward. The original source remained unchanged.

The first coverage report assembly failed on a None sentinel in stdlib trace.
Independent Phase1 reproduced the instrument issue on Python3.14; the corrected
fresh116-test author run used Python3.15 and excluded only non-positive/non-integer
line sentinels. Actual statement coverage: family68/75(90.67%), observe569/590
(96.44%), boundary427/455(93.85%). Imports were traced. Branch coverage is
NOT_MEASURED; this does not measure races or observer memory overhead.

The pipeline independently found current payload plus one reusable fixture copy
and evidence below1MiB, with limits on inaccessible earlier chronology and no
continuous high-water claim. All temporary test directories were cleaned. Nine
pending draft hashes remain unchanged. Unique evidence is retained. Storage
fell by just over2GiB during the turn; bounded checks left attribution unresolved,
with swap still14GiB and no unrelated changes. The host reserve stayed above10GiB.

Header3 appends bounded same-read parent evidence to identity records without
changing the existing row/pool caps. Larger valid observations may fail quota;
no full-run coverage guarantee follows. Attribution stays owned_unattributed
with null root. Retrospective invocation-root identity, live preflight, periodic
sampling, control publication, overhead and fresh resource/invocation reviews
remain required before the one informational diagnostic. Full LexLean/PrismPM
integration, genuine production binding and generated Pages remain required.
